title: AI Accountability Scale
subtitle: How much responsibility an author takes for a document written with LLM tools
author: Peter Kutsos
intro: The AI Accountability Scale is a system meant to help teams bring LLM tools into their everyday collaboration. By placing a document on the scale, the author gives an honest assessment of the effort they put into it and communicates that assessment to colleagues.
Recipients can then fairly decide which parts of the document to give feedback on and where to expect changes from the author first.

page.author: Author
page.committed: The author of the document you came from committed to this level by answering YES to these questions:
page.committedNone: The author of the document you came from takes no responsibility for its content. Responsibility starts at level 1 DRAFT.
page.more: The full scale and all four levels →

levels.name: FORWARDED
levels.responsibility: I take no responsibility for the content. I made no substantial changes, or I haven't read it.
levels.when: Use when the recipient has no access to LLM tools; otherwise they could have generated it themselves.

levels.name: DRAFT
levels.responsibility: The direction is relevant. I understand every sentence and can put it in my own words.
levels.when: Please respond to the direction before I start refining the details.

levels.name: VERIFIED
levels.responsibility: I know where every number comes from and I agree with every claim and conclusion.
levels.when: Please respond to the claims and arguments before I start refining the wording, layout and structure.

levels.name: SIGNED
levels.responsibility: I take responsibility for the layout, the structure and every sentence.
levels.when: I sign my name to this document and consider it finished.

questions: Have you read all of it?
Is the direction of the document relevant?
Do you understand every sentence and can you put it in your own words?
Do you know where every number comes from?
Do you agree with every claim?
Do you agree with every conclusion? Do the conclusions follow from the claims?
Is every sentence worded the way you would word it yourself?
Is the structure of the document logical and clear?
